nar.text: When it was announced that Mercedes-Benz would not start, the crowd was very disappointed. The Swiss driver Rüesch would also not start.
The starting grid was reduced to 11 cars, where positions had been decided by ballot.
Hail falls as the cars are pushed onto the grid; all run special tyres for the wet, and it is still raining at the start.
Chiron in the Alfa Romeo took the lead and shortly afterwards Stuck in an Auto Union passed into first place.
Stuck leads the first lap by 48 seconds from Chiron, with Varzi 12 seconds further back; Siena stops at the pits.
On the second lap Stuck slowed his pace, nevertheless his lead increased to 73 seconds.
Meanwhile Leiningen was able to pass Nuvolari to gain 5th place and Momberger passed Earl Howe. Siena at the tail end stopped at the pits again.
Stuck laps Pietsch; Siena does not complete the third lap.
By lap four the threatening dark clouds had moved away and the rain had stopped; the first rays of sunshine were seen in the sky.
Stuck's lead over Chiron was down to around 60 seconds and 80 seconds to Moll who had passed Varzi for third place.
On the 5th lap the track began to dry and Stuck in first place maintained his lead. Moll in the streamlined Alfa attacked Chiron in second place.
After six laps Stuck had increased his lead to 1½ minutes over Chiron with Moll following only 50 meters behind.
Chiron stops briefly and drops to third behind Moll; DePaolo retires with two broken connecting rods.
Leiningen stopped at the pits after having lost a lot of water, which he replenished.
Leiningen in fifth place retired at Kilometer marker 14 after the car lost more water, so much that he could not proceed.
Momberger who had followed Leiningen had raised his pace and passed Varzi in fourth place, relegating the Italian to fifth position.
Chiron pits for water with overheating; Momberger, on a 5m12.0s lap, takes third.
When Chiron retired at the beginning of lap 10, the field was down to seven cars.
Stuck stops for fuel and rear wheels (1m22s); Moll takes the lead. Momberger's 45-second stop lets Varzi into third.
At the end of lap 11, Moll had a lead of one minute to Stuck, who arrived slowly at the pits with a slipping clutch.
At the end of lap 12, Stuck who was fourth, reached his pit two minutes after Moll. He climbed out of his car and retired.
On lap 13, the race was still controlled by Moll, whose pace remained fast and regular. Varzi held second position ahead of Momberger's Auto Union.
Nuvolari stopped at the pits to change wheels to ensure that he would finish the race. While he was in the pits Earl Howe was able to pass the Italian into fourth place.
On the last lap the cover of his right rear tire was flung off only a few hundred meters before the finish. However, he was able continue, albeit at reduced speed.
Moll finished first ahead of Varzi and Momberger. The remaining three finishers were all lapped, Earl Howe once, Nuvolari twice and Pietsch three times.
